$comment: Hard gate for config/litellm-proxy.yaml (fleet-ops#8653). Nish 2026-09-28: no benching unless he says so. A failed row is never taken out of rotation: no bench list. Router-level cooldown_time holds a failed row for at most 60 s. Every model_list row must declare its cache capability: model_info.supports_prompt_caching (boolean) and model_info.cache_proof (non-empty string, date plus measured cached tokens or a doc link), because ~0% cache-read on four provider groups was 70% of uncached router tokens and no rule forced a new seat to say which case it is (fleet-ops#9365). router_settings.redis_host, redis_port and redis_password (os.environ/REDIS_PASSWORD) are required and redis_url is forbidden (v1.98.0 drops the password when redis_url is set; the cache has requirepass): session_affinity pins live in the Router cache, and without Redis each of the proxy's 2 worker processes keeps its own pin, so a session flips between rows with no failure (fleet-ops#9015). LiteLLM v1.98.0 never reads a redis_url under general_settings. Paid-plan rows are plain (owner roster, fleet-ops#10935, 2026-11-01): no order, weight, row cooldown or row 429-park rule lives here; a failed call is retried, then falls back. One router-level rule parks any row on its first 429 (allowed_fails_policy.RateLimitErrorAllowedFails 0), and worker-capable and its aliases retry a 429 once per other row (model_group_retry_policy), so a call walks past out-of-credit rows to a healthy one instead of failing (fleet-ops#11723: 11 of 14 worker-capable rows were out of credit, each 429 only counted toward allowed_fails 1, and a worker died on the 429). tests/test_router_dead_rows_walk.py holds both on the live config.

then.$comment: A tether row without its fallback would leave Tether unanswered on any Claude failure (Nish 2026-10-22: any Claude failure falls through to assistant).

tetherRow.$comment: Tether's Claude Sonnet 5.5 row (Nish 2026-10-22, fleet-ops#9980; 2026-10-23, Nishfleet/tether#7). The group, the model and the key are pinned together: the tether group answers only from claude-sonnet-5-5 on the Anthropic key, and that key serves no other group but review-claude (reviewClaudeRow), so no routing group or fallback other than those two reaches the prepaid credit. The row carries a 50 USD/day wall (Nish 2026-10-23), and raising it is a deliberate change with its own issue. A caller holding the proxy master key can still name the group, so Tether's own virtual key is the only key that should list it.

reviewClaudeRow.$comment: The review job's Claude row (decisions ledger 2026-11-04: the reviewer may be Claude when the builder is not). Its own group with no fallback, so a failed call ends the review instead of answering from a lane builder's family; its own 5 USD/day wall on the Anthropic key, apart from Tether's 50. Only the review runner's virtual key lists it.

workerCapableWalk.$comment: fleet-ops#11723: one 429 retry per other worker-capable row (14 rows, so 13). The cap keeps a larger value, and the long sleep it buys, out of the config.

retryPolicy.$comment: fleet-ops#9375: in-router retries must not re-send a worker prompt to a different seat more than the fallback needs. The values are locked by tests/test_router_retry_policy_no_cross_seat.py: shipped (2,2,2) produced a third in-group pick that re-sent the whole prompt cold; the #9375 cut caps the worker group before the fallback group (or Pi's own retry, which keeps the session id and therefore the pin). On litellm 1.98.0 the one allowed retry goes back to the row that just failed when that row is still healthy after the 429 (router allowed_fails 1; the test drills it). A row that parks on its first 429 (RateLimitErrorAllowedFails 0, the daily-quota rows) is already cooling, so its retry goes to a peer: still capped at one extra pick, not a same-row retry. Either way the cap removes the third-seat re-send. A litellm upgrade can change that, which is why the test pins the version. ContentPolicyViolationErrorRetries is 0 because a content-policy refusal repeats on every seat; AuthenticationErrorRetries is 1 (fleet-ops#10756) because a 401 does not recover on the same row but the router-level AuthenticationErrorAllowedFails 0 (config/litellm-proxy.yaml router_settings.allowed_fails_policy, required at 0 by this schema) parks the 401 row on its first failure, so the granted retry goes to a live peer in the same group and one dead provider key does not fail the whole session. TimeoutErrorRetries/InternalServerErrorRetries/BadRequestErrorRetries are capped at 1 (InternalServerErrorRetries is inert on 1.98.0: get_num_retries_from_retry_policy has no InternalServerError branch, so it was a forward bound only, and it went live with the v1.105.0 image move (fleet-ops#10071). fleet-ops#9050 adds NotFoundErrorRetries and DefaultRetries, both live on 1.105.0: the policy is read before should_retry_this_error, NotFoundErrorRetries covers a status-404 answer, and DefaultRetries covers every class the policy does not name (a 402 maps to APIError with no named key; a 403 from an openai-compatible provider arrives as BadRequestError carrying status 403, which BadRequestErrorRetries already granted on both 1.98.0 and 1.105.0). Whether the granted retry reaches a different row depends on rotation: a 404 parks the row on NotFoundErrorAllowedFails 0, so the retry went to a live peer; a 403 cools nothing, so the session pin overrides the skip list and the granted attempt re-picks the same row (both drilled on 1.105.0 in tests/test_router_retry_policy_no_cross_seat.py). Both are capped at 1 like the other retry keys; named keys keep precedence, so content-policy stays 0 and a 429 gets the second, peer-row retry. RateLimitErrorRetries is capped at 2 in router_settings.retry_policy (fleet-ops#10178: the second retry runs after the pinned row is parked and lands on a peer, so a one-slot row that is full does not leak a 429 from a group with no fallback). model_group_retry_policy lifts it for worker-capable alone (fleet-ops#11723): every 429 now parks its row, so each extra retry lands on a row not yet tried, and the walk needs one retry per other row; a 429 is refused before the model reads the prompt, so a walked row costs no work. All keys are required and unknown keys are forbidden on purpose: a new litellm knob must arrive as a reviewed schema change, not a silent config edit.

allOf.$comment: fleet-ops#10608 (Nish 2026-10-28): GLM-5.3-Flash is a worker model only and Qwen is a judge or reviewer only. A GLM-5.3-Flash row in any group but a worker group, or a Qwen row in a worker group, fails here. pilot is the gh-aw pilot's worker group (fleet-ops#11311).

Tether's Claude row: every row named tether is the pinned row, every row on the Anthropic key is the tether row or the review-claude row, and there is at most one of each, so a second tether row, a tether row on another model or provider, or the Anthropic key on another group all fail here. Absence is allowed (the schema's own reject cases are built without it); router_settings.fallbacks requires tether -> assistant whenever the row exists.

model_info.$comment: fleet-ops#9365: cache_proof is checked for presence and non-emptiness only, so the gate catches a missing verdict but does not read the text - 'unknown' would pass. That is deliberate: a pattern demanding a date and a token count would reject the legitimate 'cannot cache, here is the vendor doc' proof. What holds a hollow claim down is the proof line being a real measurement a reviewer can re-derive, and the probe behind it being quoted on the PR.

model_group_alias.$comment: fleet-ops#9330 desk arm of the 3-day token trial, and nothing else: an alias renames a group Pi already picks, so Pi's compaction.modelOverrides (keyed provider/model) can shorten that arm's context without moving a single call to another seat. Only a worker group a Pi job can pick has one, which is why worker-public is here and assistant is not. One exception: judge -> assistant keeps the old judge callers answered after the judge group was deleted (fleet-ops#10935). Pinned as a closed map because an alias also renames the fallback chain: Router._get_model_from_alias resolves the name before routing, but fallback_lookup_groups keys on the requested name, so an alias with no fallbacks entry of its own inherits nothing and a failed row ends the call (the 'No fallback model group' shape of fleet-ops#9290). tests/test_workflow_caps.py asserts each pair here is real, that no alias name shadows a model_name, and that the desk name agent.yml builds is listed.

fallbacks.$comment: Tether: the tether entry is exactly [assistant] (a Claude failure falls to the group Hermes already uses, never to a worker group or back), and no other group may fall into tether. review-claude neither falls back nor is fallen into, so the Claude credit is spent only by Tether and the review job. W10c: worker-capable is the strong group and never falls down, so no worker-capable entry may name worker-cheap, worker-public or assistant; a strong call with no healthy row fails at the caller.

optional_pre_call_checks.description: Must contain session_affinity. Without that pre-call check the router never runs DeploymentAffinityCheck, so a session pin cannot exist, every call in a session shuffles across vendors and the prompt cache never hits (fleet-ops#9361).

allowed_fails_policy.$comment: fleet-ops#10756, #11723: with allowed_fails set, LiteLLM counts a 401 or 429 toward it instead of cooling the row at once (docs.litellm.ai/docs/routing, When are deployments cooled down). Both keys are required at 0, so every row parks on its first 401 or 429 and the granted retry goes to a peer.

model_group_retry_policy.$comment: fleet-ops#11723: worker-capable has no fallback (W10c), so its 429 retries walk the group. The policy is keyed by the requested name, so an alias with no entry of its own gets retry_policy (drilled on 1.105.0). Closed to worker-capable and its aliases: a single-row group with 13 retries sleeps 92 s before its fallback (drilled with tether).
